summary: REFACTOR REGRESSION VALIDATION (iteration 18) — Backend monolith server.py was split into 6 modular routers in /app/backend/routes/ (inventory, sales, accounts_receivable, expenses, commissions, reports). Goal: zero functional regression. RESULT: 100% pass on all 6 refactored modules (124/124 pytest tests). Non-refactored modules: 119/130 pass; 11 failures in legacy modules are pre-existing test-vs-implementation mismatches, NOT regressions caused by the refactor. Frontend smoke E2E: login OK, all 9 dashboard tabs (Dashboard, Agenda, Pacientes, Inventario, Ventas, Cuentas, Gastos, Comisiones, Reportes) load with content and no on-page errors; only 1 React 'unique key prop' warning in AgendaPage. Backend startup is clean (no import errors). server.py loads routes in correct order (inventory → expenses → commissions → sales → accounts_receivable → reports) so the EXPENSE_CATEGORY_LABELS cross-import resolves. Performed 124 endpoint calls across all 6 refactored modules + URL/structure parity with iterations 11-17 baselines. Refactor verified safe.

Returns 500 instead of 404 for invalid patient_id — PRE-EXISTING (medical_records in server.py).
Test asserts legacy key 'total_patients' but response has 'new_patients_month'. Stale test (test_clinic_agenda.py line 106) — endpoint behaviour unchanged.
Test asserts list shape but endpoint correctly returns paginated {patients, page, pages, limit}. Stale test.

issues: React console warning: 'Each child in a list should have a unique key prop' rendered from AgendaPage. Pre-existing, not blocking. Recommend adding stable keys to the offending list.

action_items: REFACTOR IS SAFE — no regression. Main agent can ship.

critical_code_review_comments: Refactor is well-executed: import order (expenses before reports) correctly handles EXPENSE_CATEGORY_LABELS cross-module dependency. /app/backend/routes/__init__.py is empty which means routes are imported as `from routes import inventory, ...` from server.py — works because /app/backend is the working dir; ensure pytest/unitenv also has it on sys.path (already does).
server.py is still 3472 lines — large but ~43% smaller than before. Could continue extracting auth/agenda/patients/prescriptions/lab_orders into their own routers using the same pattern.

commissions.py exposes _compute_commissions_for_sale and is imported by sales.py — this is fine, but note it creates a circular-import risk if commissions ever needs to import from sales. Currently safe because commissions only imports from server (auth dependencies) and stdlib.
reports.py imports EXPENSE_CATEGORY_LABELS from routes.expenses — clean dependency direction (reports depends on expenses).
All 6 routers correctly use APIRouter with consistent /clinic/* prefixes and feature-flag dependencies.
No data-shape/parity issues found compared to iterations 11-17 baselines.
seed_data_creation: None — used existing fixtures created by previous iterations (1 cash session open, sales Q9600 incl Q500, 1 commission Q150, 1 AR with 3-installment plan, 1 expense Q3136 alquiler, 14+ sales in fixture set).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Refactor iteration 18 verified zero regression. The 6 refactored modules (inventory/sales/AR/expenses/commissions/reports) are now in /app/backend/routes/ and have 100% pytest pass. server.py is 3472 lines and still hosts auth/agenda/patients/prescriptions/lab_orders/branches/settings/members/medical_records — these were untouched and behave identically. Frontend was not modified and works end-to-end. The 11 pre-existing failures in legacy tests are NOT refactor regressions; they are stale-test-assertion or 500-vs-404 normalization issues that existed before the refactor. Future refactor iterations can continue extracting more modules using the same pattern (cross-imports must respect router order in server.py).
rca of the issue: N/A — no regressions. Pre-existing minor issues documented above for awareness but unrelated to the refactor.
